subject: Data handling: split TTL pilot & residency check
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma Reynolds <emma@thelumenlab.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Data handling: split TTL pilot & residency check

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same picture: 

Summary of Lumen Lab requirements from discovery:
- High-level: you must avoid persisting free-text user prompts (PII-sensitive) beyond the session.
- KV/session state can be retained for session continuity, but limited window preferred (you mentioned ~7 days).
- Audit/debug traces should be available to your Ops team but stored hashed/anonymized and kept separate from raw payloads.
- Data residency: EU-only storage for logs/derived telemetry (model weights can remain hosted in our global infra if needed).
- Compliance: SOC 2 + evidence for key controls and ability to turn on customer-managed KMS.

Proposed Redwood approach (short):
1) Split retention model: ephemeral full-payload retention = 0 (no raw prompt persistence),
   KV cache retained for 7 days to reduce cold-start latency and keep session context,
   hashed debug traces (SHA256 digests + timestamp) retained 90 days for investigation.
2) Region lock: logs/derived telemetry stored in EU region; keys under customer KMS possible.
3) Access & audit: role-based access, exportable audit logs, and a signed SOW addendum for pilot parameters.

Attached: retention_matrix.xlsx (matrix of options) — please review and mark which rows are mandatory vs. negotiable.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm which two items are non-negotiable (e.g., 0 raw retention, EU residency),
- We spin up a 2-week pilot with the split model (canary variant) and provide a short SOW + DocuSign link.

If that sounds right I’ll loop in Marissa from Legal to draft the SOW language and Ben (Solutions) to scope the pilot runbook.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: retention_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: Emma Reynolds <emma@thelumenlab.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data handling: split TTL pilot & residency check

Hi Soojin —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few immediate clarifications from the Lumen Lab security/legal side: 

1) Zero raw-payload retention is a must for Product (we cannot allow raw prompts to persist outside the active session for more than 0 minutes).
2) For auditability we do need traces, but those must be anonymized and hashed; we cannot accept any reversible form of raw payload in the debug traces.
3) EU residency for logs/derived telemetry is mandatory; we also require encryption-at-rest using our KMS (we can share key material or KMS ARN).
4) We need to understand what guarantees Redwood can give in an SLA for deletion (e.g., confirm deletion workflows and retention windows).

Can you confirm whether the 7-day KV cache can be restricted to EU region and whether session continuity will break if we require stricter isolation for some customers? Also please send a sample SOW and the SLA language we should expect for deletion and proof of deletion.

If you can get Ben to outline the technical controls and Marissa to propose the SOW wording, we can route this internally for a yes/no on the pilot.

Thanks — I’ll prioritize review once we have the sample docs.

—
Emma Reynolds
Head of AI Ops, The Lumen Lab
emma@thelumenlab.com | +44 20 7946 0991
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Reynolds <emma@thelumenlab.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data handling: split TTL pilot & residency check

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the precise list — that helps. Below is a practical mapping of controls we can deliver for the pilot and what would require contract language: 

Option A (recommended pilot - minimal friction):
- Full-payload ephemeral pipeline: application traffic routed through a transient buffer; raw prompts are not written to persistent storage. Tokens used for inference are discarded after model invocation.
- KV/session cache: stored in EU region, TTL = 7 days (configurable down to 0), encrypted with customer-provided KMS.
- Debug traces: store only SHA256 digests of input + timestamp + error codes; no reversible data. Retention 90 days, accessible via telemetry export.
- Proof of deletion: job-based purge with audit entries; we can provide signed deletion receipts for pilot runs.

Option B (stricter, enterprise):
- Support for policy-based sandboxing per-account (isolated tenant storage + dedicated KMS).
- 0-day KV retention (session-only, memory-resident) for regulated customers — increases cold-start and may require dedicated capacity.

Attachments: I attached a populated retention_matrix.xlsx with the EU-locked KV row flagged, and a sample_sow_redwood_v1.docx with draft wording for deletion clauses, KMS integration, and pilot scope.

If you’re good to proceed we suggest:
1) Pilot scope: 2 weeks, EU-region KV = 7 days, debug traces = hashed-only, customer KMS enabled.
2) Deliverables: pilot runbook + deletion receipts + sample SLA paragraph.
3) Legal: Marissa, can you propose SOW language for the deletion confirmation and KMS terms?

Emma — note that Option B (0-day KV) will need a short design doc and potentially Reserved capacity if the performance hit is unacceptable. We can sketch that next week if needed.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

Soojin / Ben / Marissa —

This all looks good as a starting point. We approve the 2-week pilot under Option A with these conditions: EU-locked KV at 7 days, debug traces hashed-only, and customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest. Legal wants the deletion receipt language in the SOW and a short SLA paragraph that specifies our right to request proof of deletion within 30 days of request.

Please send the DocuSign and the pilot runbook and I’ll route internally — expect a go/no-go within 48 hours after review.

Thanks,
Emma
